I am 74 years old and have farmed these 3 mu in Quzhou for half a century. I know every inch of this land. My wife and I manage the farm together, and we rely on the wheat-maize double crop because that is what the North China Plain gives us. We have well water, so we can irrigate when the rains fail, but I do not waste water or money on inputs we do not need.

For wheat, I will sow an improved variety in early October right after rotary tillage. I will spread compound fertilizer as a base dressing and top-dress with urea at the jointing stage in spring. In total, that comes to about 15 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times from my well: once before winter freeze to protect the seedlings, once at jointing, and once at heading. I will spray herbicide once after sowing and fungicide once in late spring if the humidity rises. With good weather, I expect around 480 kg per mu.

For maize, time is tight after the wheat comes off in early June. I will sow hybrid maize seed directly into the stubble without ploughing—no-tillage keeps moisture and saves labor when the summer heat is pressing. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress nitrogen at the big trumpet stage, for about 14 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice, at the jointing/big trumpet stage and during grain filling. Two pesticide sprays will handle weeds and corn borer. I expect about 550 kg per mu.
